subject: Approval requested: revenue split carveout & licensing term alignment for ACME private offer
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Patricia Lopez <patricia.lopez@acme.com>, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Approval requested: revenue split carveout & licensing term alignment for ACME private offer

Team —

Quick background: ACME is pushing a private listing for a multi-cloud trial (primarily AWS, will list on GCP later) with an initial committed spend roughly $1.2M over year 1 and an expected expansion path. They want two non-standard items in the private offer: a reduced rev-share to 18% (our standard for marketplace listings is 25%) and a 3-year licensing commitment term (our preference is 12 months for private offers). They also want Net60 payment terms and a small onboarding credit. ACME is strategic (large retail customer) and the AWS marketplace listing will materially increase visibility for us in the vertical.

Attached: ACME_PrivateOffer_Terms_v3.pdf (redlines from their legal), deal_summary_ACME.xlsx.

Asking: I want to surface this for executive carveout approval — specifically:
- Approve rev-share at 18% for AWS private listing for initial 12 months, reverting to 22% thereafter (or alternative guidance)
- Approve 3-year license term but with annual true-ups and a 12-month enforceable minimum in year 1
- Allow Net60 for first 12 months given procurement constraints, with Finance holdback if payment delinquencies occur
- Approve a one-time onboarding credit up to $40k

Why: Win is strategic, visible, and likely to accelerate other retail deals on marketplace. Risks: lower unit economics up-front, longer contract commitment increases exposure to churn, and additional billing complexity with Net60. Karthik — can you provide a short margin impact calc? Lauren — can you confirm legal redline risks that would require further escalation? Marissa — requesting your OK / conditional sign-off.

Thanks,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: ACME_PrivateOffer_Terms_v3.pdf (PDF, 312KB); deal_summary_ACME.xlsx (XLSX, 54KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Approval requested: revenue split carveout & licensing term alignment for ACME private offer

Rafael —

Reviewed the numbers quickly. Rough sketch: with a 18% rev-share vs 25% on $1.2M run rate we give up ~ $84k in marketplace payout over year 1 compared to standard. If we model the 3-year term with annual true-ups and expect 30% expansion in year 2, the long-term ARR lift counters an initial margin dip but depends heavily on retention and upsell timing. The onboarding credit at $40k is significant but could be staged against milestones (50% on launch, 50% on first 90d active usage).

Recommendations:
- Approve conditional 18% for AWS for first 12 months only; require conversion to at least 22% in year 2 unless we hit agreed expansion thresholds (deal_summary has candidate milestones).
- Require Finance to pre-authorize Net60 but flag with PO and require invoice escalation plan. If payment falls >30 days past Net60, revert to Net30 for subsequent invoices and assess holdback.
- Onboarding credit to be milestone-based and capped at $30k unless Marissa approves the full $40k.

I'll attach a quick margin delta tab to the HubSpot deal. If Execs want a cleaner ask, I can convert to a single-slide impact and a fallback plan.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Patricia Lopez <patricia.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Approval requested: revenue split carveout & licensing term alignment for ACME private offer

Team —

I reviewed ACME's redlines (see attached redlines_ACME_legal.docx). Key legal/contract risks to flag:
- Three year term increases exposure and ACME insists on automatic renewal clauses. We should replace automatic renewal with explicit renewal based on consumption thresholds or minimum commitment triggers.
- Their indemnity language asks for broader IP carveouts; we cannot accept without senior legal sign-off.
- Payment net terms: Net60 for a first-year strategic customer is okay if Finance mitigates credit risk with a PO and a staggered payment/usage tie-out.

Suggested guardrails for exec approval:
1) Approve commercial carveouts (18% rev-share + milestone-based onboarding credit up to $30k) conditionally if Legal signs off on: no automatic multi-year renewals, a vendor-friendly IP/indemnity clause, and an audit right reserved for us.
2) Approve the 3-year term only if we insert 12-month minimum commitment language and annual price/usage true-ups.
3) One-time finance holdback clause triggered on late payment beyond Net90.

If Execs want to keep the full economics (18% + $40k credit), Legal will need explicit escalation to General Counsel for the IP/indemnity language; otherwise we can accept the 30k capped credit and the conditional language above.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Patricia Lopez <patricia.lopez@acme.com>, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Approval requested: revenue split carveout & licensing term alignment for ACME private offer

Thanks for the diligence — Rafael, Karthik, Lauren. I’ll approve the commercial carveouts with the following binding conditions:

1) Rev-share: 18% for the first 12 months only, reverting to 22% in year 2 unless ACME hits the expansion milestones outlined in the deal_summary (we will codify the milestones in the SOW).
2) Term: Approve the 3-year term only with an explicit 12-month minimum in year 1 and annual true-ups (pricing/usage reconciliation) otherwise we reserve termination for material breach or non-payment. No automatic multi-year renewals without explicit notice and consent.
3) Onboarding credit: approve up to $30k staged against two milestones (launch + 90d active usage). If Rafael can justify the additional $10k (quantified ROI tied to AWS marketplace uplift within 6 months), I will consider the incremental credit with GC sign-off on indemnity language.
4) Net60: Finance to accept Net60 for year 1 but require a PO and a credit check; late payment beyond Net90 triggers a finance holdback and reversion to Net30.
5) Legal: Lauren to finalize redlines removing broad IP indemnities and adding our audit clause; any remaining risk items must be escalated to GC.

Rafael — please update the HubSpot deal with these conditions, confirm milestone language in the SOW, and get the DocuSign packet ready. Karthik — please capture the final margin delta and ensure Finance has the PO details. Lauren — loop in GC if ACME pushes on indemnities.

Conditional approval granted. Keep me posted on any pushback.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
VP, Global Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Forwarded message included for ACME and AWS Marketplace.
Attachments: redlines_ACME_legal.docx (DOCX, 28KB)
